$comment: Schema for the collections CommentsKit reads and writes. Nothing applies this file for you: create the collections and fields with your backend's own tools (the DaaS MCP / Studio, or the Engine equivalent), then create EVERY foreign key with a relation call (a field with a relation block does not create the constraint). Replace <host> with the collection being commented on (ticket, document, order...). Column names follow the add-comments skill (buildpad-ai/skills); itemsAdapter's `fields` option maps other names.

collections.note: One row per comment or reply. The create hook stamps author, root, access and created_at; the browser sends only host, parent, body and photos.

fields.note: The thing commented on. Pass this column name as itemsAdapter's hostField.
The comment answered; null on a top-level comment
The first comment of the thread; null on a top-level comment. Stamped by the hook as parent.root ?? parent.id. Backfill it for existing replies before the kit reads them.
Stamped by the hook, never sent by the browser
Plain-text markup: **bold**, *italic*, ++underline++, '- ' bullets. Up to 20 000 characters (the hook trims and bounds it). May be empty only when photos is non-empty.

List of file ids (from POST /api/files), null when none, at most 20. The hook should check it is a list of at most 20 strings. A picture alone is a valid comment, so body may be empty when photos is not. Deleting a comment does not delete its files.
Only if you want Resolve/Reopen on top-level comments. Pass fields.resolved: 'resolved' to itemsAdapter.

relations.note: CASCADE, not the add-comments skill's SET NULL: the kit's delete asks 'Delete this comment and its replies?', so the replies must go with it. With SET NULL they would turn into top-level comments.

collections.note: One row per person per emoji per comment, from the fixed list of twelve. Reactions send no email.

fields.note: One of 👍 👎 ❤️ 🎉 😄 😮 😢 🙏 👀 🚀 ✅ 🔥. The hook compares with the variation selector removed and stores the list's form.
Stamped by the hook. Never name this column 'user': it is reserved.

alias.note: Lets one read nest reactions.id, reactions.emoji and reactions.reacted_by with the comment

indexes.note: Stops two quick clicks inserting a duplicate

<host>_comments.read: By the same rule as the thing commented on
<host>_comments.create: Only the fields the browser sends: <host>, parent, body, photos. A view-only person may reply but not start a thread, if your app wants that rule (enforce it in the hook).
<host>_comments.update: None by default (comments are immutable). If you enable itemsAdapter's allowEdit, allow update of body where author = $CURRENT_USER.
<host>_comments.delete: None by default. If you enable allowDelete: author = $CURRENT_USER, plus a moderator rule (a module access key, checked with hasModuleAccess, not a role name).

hooks: The create hooks (comments and reactions) are written once per project: see the add-comments skill, step 3. They use only services.items.
proof: Create a throwaway comment with a reply and a reaction, delete the parent, and count the child rows. Reading the relation does not show on_delete, so a delete test is the only proof the cascade exists.
